podcast.body: A single by Pure Prairie League that was noted for attracting younger listeners to their music. "a lot of younger people are picking up on our music now because of the single Amy."

srcs.episode: Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.body: Originally a cut from the 1972 album "Bustin' Out," "Amy" gained traction through college radio play before being picked up by country and then Top 40 stations. RCA re-signed Pure Prairie League and re-released it as a single, giving the band "new life." It peaked at #27 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1975 and is characterized by twang, harmonies, and heartache. Co-founder Craig Fuller described it simply as "just a song," an "exercise in song craftsmanship." "Amy made it to only number 27 on the billboard hot one hundred and nineteen seventy five"
